thread:
Alex Kim: Quick kickoff — I'm refactoring our internal incident comms templates to make them tighter for on-call handoffs and clearer for customer-facing updates. Goal: one succinct public line + optional appendix. Share quick reactions.

Priya Rao: Love the direction. One constraint: customer email should have a 1-2 sentence summary up top, then an optional detail block. Customers want immediate clarity.

Ben Hooper: Agree. Also propose we standardize incident IDs as RID-YYMMDD-#### so logs and git branches are easy to scan.

Casey Nguyen: Drafted a minimal internal template for quick pager-to-pager handoffs. Keeping it razor-short so the new oncall can act immediately.

Casey Nguyen: ```
MINIMAL INTERNAL TEMPLATE (for handoffs):
- Incident ID: {incident_id}
- One-line summary: what failed + affected surface
- Impact snapshot: who/what, rough scale (eg ~7% requests, region: eu-west)
- Current status: Investigating / Mitigating / Resolved
- Immediate actions & owners: bullet list (who is doing what)
- Next ETA/update: {next_update_at}
- Quick links: runbook, recent logs, dashboard
- Data exposure: yes/no/unknown
```

Grace Li: Can we add a single public-facing snippet field (<140 chars) for status page / header? Makes automation easier.

Alex Kim: Added. Below is the paired internal + external copy I propose. Comments welcome.

Alex Kim: ```
INTERNAL - FULL (for major incidents):
- Incident ID: {incident_id}
- Short summary (1 line)
- Severity: P1 / P2
- Impact: {affected_percent} of requests, {features_impacted}, {regions}
- Detected: {detected_at}
- Current status: Investigating / Mitigating / Resolved
- Hypothesis / suspected cause: single line
- Actions in flight: 1) owner - task, 2) owner - task
- Workarounds: short note if available
- ETA / next update: {next_update_at}
- Handoff tips: last commands, dev/tag, recent config edits, where to check canary metrics
- Data exposure: yes/no/unknown (if yes, page Security immediately)
- Communication plan: cadence for internal updates, who drafts public blurb, email/targeted notifications

PUBLIC STATUS SNIPPET (mandatory for P1 within 30m):
- Blurb (<140 chars): {public_blurb}
- Details (status page): short paragraphs, Impact header first, avoid tech jargon

CUSTOMER EMAIL TEMPLATE (top two lines required):
Subject: [Redwood] Incident {incident_id}: {short-impact-summary}
Hi {customer_name},
We are aware of an issue affecting {feature/region}. Our engineers are working on mitigation; next update by {next_update_at}.
(OPTIONAL DETAILS BELOW)
We have taken the following steps: {brief mitigations}. If you need immediate assistance contact {support_contact}.
Sincerely,
Redwood Inference Ops
```

Maya S.: Tone note: avoid definitive words like "fixed" until verified. Use "mitigated" or "service appears restored" and confirm in follow-up. Also recommend a one-line "notify decision" field: Notify: yes/no/key-stakeholders only.

Ben Hooper: Add a short severity guidance snippet to reduce ambiguity: P1 = service outage or >10% users impacted; P2 = degraded performance for subset; P3 = isolated error with workaround.

Priya Rao: Security ask: make the Data exposure row mandatory for any path touching customer data. That drives prompt escalation.

incident-bot: Reminder: templates live on branch incident-comms/redraft-2026. Use `/incident template populate RID-XXXX` to replace placeholders. Enforcement: soft warning when public_blurb missing on P1s for 2 weeks, then enforced. :robot_face:

Alex Kim: Also adding a short on-call handoff snippet to the bottom so shift changes are clean. Suggest this appears in the PR description too.

Casey Nguyen: ```
ONCALL HANDOFF (2-line snapshot):
- State: Mitigating; rollback started at {time}; traffic shifted to {region}
- New oncall actions: check {dashboard_link}, validate mitigation, contact {owner} if alerts > threshold
```

Grace Li: Small UX ask: auto-populate {status_page_link} and {incident_id} when rendering templates in the incident app so comms lead doesn't need to copy.

Ben Hooper: Quick examples for public blurbs (paste these in PR comments):
- "Partial disruption to embeddings in eu-west; engineers investigating. Next update 14:45 UTC."
- "Were investigating increased error rates for API requests in us-east; mitigation in progress."

Maya S.: Agree on examples; also add a short reminder to not paste secrets or customer PII in Slack. If data exposure = yes, follow the breach playbook and notify Security.

Alex Kim: I'll open the PR with these templates and the enforcement policy. Please add blurbs and a couple sample filled templates for a P1 and P2. Planning to merge in ~24h unless there are blocking objections.

Priya Rao: LGTM from Product side.

Ben Hooper: +1. Will drop a few example blurbs shortly.

incident-bot: Policy note scheduled: public_blurb enforcement for P1s will be a soft warning for 14 days, then strict. Use `/incident policy view` for details.

Alex Kim: Thanks everyone — closing thread after PR. If you don't leave feedback in the PR within 24h I'll ping relevant owners.
